clues.title: Google car: Unique car
text: This gray Street View car with a visible roof rack and mirrors is unique to Guatemala. Don’t confuse it with the Dominican Republic car, which has black stripes on the roof rack, or the Curaçao car, which has a black front. A similar car is found in Laos, so always check the surroundings before making a guess.

clues.title: Pole: Green poles
text: All-green painted metal poles can be found in only a few areas of Guatemala, mostly in the Southeast of the country. They have codes on them that will tell you even more precisely where you are.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Road line: Roadlines
text: Similarly to Mexico, Guatemalan roads generally have solid white outer lines with a single yellow middle line.
Road lines in Guatemala are generally significantly thinner than in Mexico.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Stop sign: Alto
text: Guatemala, Panama, Costa Rica and Mexico are the only countries using the word "Alto" on their stop signs.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Painted Poles
text: In Guatemala you will very commonly see poles painted with either pink, green or a combination of the two.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Unique Car
text: This grey Street View car with a visible roof rack and side mirrors can be seen on all car coverage in Guatemala.
The only other tropical country with a similar car is Laos.

clues.title: Landscape: Lago de Atitlán
text: Lago de Atitlán is by far the largest lake in the mountainous regions of Guatemala. It is surrounded by mountains, and some volcanoes.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Mountains
text: The central regions of Guatemala are generally mountainous.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: North
text: The northern regions of Guatemala are typically fairly flat. You will however usually see some hills or a slightly rolling landscape, rather than the complete flatness of the south.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: South
text: The southern regions of Guatemala mainly consist of completely flat agricultural land. It is generally more built up than flat areas in the north.

clues.title: Architecture: Pastel Stone Houses
text: Guatemalan architecture mainly consists of pastel painted stone houses, commonly with rusted sheet metal roofs.
It is also somewhat common for buildings to be made out of exposed white brick.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: completely green pole
text: Completely green utility poles are primarily found in the southeast of the country, but also on a road in the further north in the east and on a small stretch of road around Melchor de Mencos, near the end of the coverage in the far northeast.
These poles also feature small pole plates, which can further narrow down the road. This will be further explained in the next tip.
